sources.locator: Contents (PDF p. 1); §4.3 `Monomial Groups`, printed pp. 57-58 / PDF pp. 56-58; and §4.6 `Induction Theorems`, printed pp. 63-66 / PDF pp. 62-65. The latter range is read through Proposition 4.6.9 and its two problems.

contents.name: Contents entries `4.3 Monomial Groups` and `4.6 Induction Theorems`
4.3 `Monomial Groups` (definitions of monomial representation/group and supersolvable group)
Proposition 4.3.2 (faithful irreducibles with a noncentral abelian normal subgroup induce from a proper subgroup)
Lemma 4.3.3 (a nonabelian supersolvable group has a noncentral normal abelian subgroup)
Lemma 4.3.4 (induction is compatible with lifting along a quotient)
Problem 4.3.1 (the binary tetrahedral group has a nonmonomial faithful representation)
contents.reason: This is a nonmonomial solvable-group counterexample for the later page devoted to monomial characters and M-groups, not a prerequisite of the elementary-subgroup induction proof.

contents.name: Theorem 4.6.1 (the hyperelementary permutation relation)
contents.reason: The text explicitly defers this proof, and the design explicitly forbids resting this page on that unproved relation; Li and Kramár supply the proved replacement route.

contents.name: Theorem 4.6.2 (hyperelementary induction)
contents.reason: Its proof is stated as a consequence of the preceding deferred permutation relation, so using it would violate the page's chosen fully proved Li/Kramár route.

contents.name: Theorem 4.6.3 (monomial induction)
contents.reason: The general generation theorem for monomial representations belongs to the later M-group page; only its narrower elementary-group prerequisite is established locally here.

contents.name: Proposition 4.6.7 (descent from a scalar-extension direct summand)
contents.reason: This scalar-extension descent statement is a central ingredient of the immediately later fields-of-definition page and is not needed to state the cyclotomic splitting corollary here.

contents.name: Proposition 4.6.8 (restriction to elementary subgroups is a split injection)
Problem 4.6.1 (verify elementary induction for $A_5$)
contents.reason: The assigned examples page instead gives the smaller complete $S_3$ calculation; this source problem is an unworked exercise and would require a separate $A_5$ subgroup analysis.

contents.name: Problem 4.6.2 (the $A_5$ virtual permutation relation using dihedral subgroups)
contents.reason: This hyperelementary permutation relation uses noncyclic dihedral subgroups and is not the cyclic-integrality counterexample, whose degree-parity proof is built independently on the examples page.
